stem.dissection.diagram_unavailable: The enlarged view could not open. Diagram description:
stem.dissection.diagram_pan_hint: At larger sizes, scroll inside the diagram. Keyboard: focus the diagram area and use the arrow keys. Escape closes this view.
stem.dissection.diagram_scope: Reference study only. Zoom changes the drawing size, not specimen measurements or observation credit.
stem.dissection.spatial_scope: These are schematic 2D study views. Depth shading helps orientation; it is not measured 3D anatomy.
stem.dissection.spatial_axis_symbols: Circle = first landmark; diamond = opposite landmark.
stem.dissection.spatial_isolated: For this isolated organ, use these landmarks to orient yourself. The view names identify illustration presets, not a validated rotation of a scanned organ.
stem.dissection.spatial_body: Use the specimen’s anatomical directions rather than assuming that screen-left is the animal’s left.
stem.dissection.spatial_question: Before changing view, predict which landmark will stay in place and which structures may become obscured.
stem.dissection.spatial_layer_detail: Changing view keeps the current layer and your evidence. The Internal preset does not cut tissue, complete preparation, or unlock deeper layers.
stem.dissection.spatial_map_detail: The layer map shows the activity sequence, not tissue thickness or a true anatomical cross-section.
stem.dissection.essentials_workspace_kee: Essentials workspace: keeps the procedure, instruments, observation, evidence, assessment, and accessibility controls in focus.
stem.dissection.advanced_workspace_adds_: Advanced workspace: adds scenarios, detailed telemetry, technique comparison, instructor settings, and extended visualization tools.
stem.dissection.recall_scope: Practice is separate from observed evidence and assessment scores. Drafts and self-ratings last for this activity; opening flashcards again or changing layers starts fresh.
stem.dissection.recall_task: What does this structure do? Explain its main role in your own words. Say, sign, sketch, or write your answer.
stem.dissection.recall_check: Did your answer explain the main function? Look for a missing idea or a correction; exact wording is not required.
stem.dissection.recall_summary: These are your self-ratings, not a mastery score. Revisit uncertain cards, then test your explanation against the specimen and your notes.
stem.dissection.recall_empty_hint: Return to the specimen and choose an available layer.
stem.dissection.comparison_unmapped: No cross-specimen comparison is mapped for this structure. Similar names alone do not establish a valid anatomical comparison.
stem.dissection.comparison_reference_lim: Reading these references does not mark other specimens as observed. Record one supported similarity, one difference, and what you would need to inspect next.
stem.dissection.comparison_write: Write comparison in my evidence note
stem.dissection.structure_layer_or_words: Structure, layer, or words in your note
stem.dissection.observe_first_prompt: Record one visible feature and where it is in the evidence note below. Open the reference whenever you need support, then revise anything the comparison changes.
stem.dissection.reference_context_help: Reference context can extend your learning. Base the evidence note on features and anatomical relationships you can observe in this specimen.
stem.dissection.model_scope_detail: This is a schematic learning model. Colors, sizes, motion, and layer boundaries help you study; they are not measurements or a histology slide.
stem.dissection.trace_connection: Trace a connection in this specimen
stem.dissection.connection_exposure: reveal or change view to inspect.
stem.dissection.connection_unmapped: No connection is mapped for this structure. Use its location and the specimen reference to propose one.
stem.dissection.confidence_not_sure_yet_: Inspect one more visible feature and its location.
stem.dissection.confidence_somewhat_sure: Check one more distinguishing feature or anatomical relationship.
stem.dissection.confidence_confident_cue: Check that each claim in your note matches what you actually observed.
stem.dissection.countercheck_starter_tex: I would revise this identification if I observed
stem.dissection.draft_review_observe_cue: Describe a feature you can see in this model. Schematic color, size, or motion is not a measurement of a real specimen.
stem.dissection.draft_review_locate_cue: State where the feature is and how it relates to another visible structure. Use the specimen orientation to check directions.
stem.dissection.draft_review_explain_cue: Explain how your observations support the identification. Name any reference you used and separate its claims from what you saw.
stem.dissection.countercheck_starter_add: Countercheck starter added. Finish the sentence in your evidence note.
stem.dissection.confidence_question: How sure are you, based on your evidence?
stem.dissection.confidence_default_cue: Choose based on the evidence in your note, not on how familiar the answer feels.
stem.dissection.draft_check_limit: Text and confidence are recorded separately. Their presence does not verify the explanation or earn an assessment score.
stem.dissection.countercheck_prompt: What different feature, location, or connection would make this identification less likely—or suggest a different structure?
stem.dissection.countercheck_finish: Finish the countercheck sentence in your evidence note.
stem.dissection.countercheck_ungraded: Optional reflection; no effect on observation credit or assessment scores.
stem.dissection.directory_scope: Filters apply to this layer. Recorded means a note and confidence are present, not verified mastery.
stem.dissection.no_filter_matches: No structures match this progress filter. Choose All structures or clear the filters.
stem.dissection.no_layer_structures: No structures are listed in this layer.
stem.dissection.reference_discovery_help: These are reference matches. Opening a layer does not mark a structure as inspected.
stem.dissection.layer_prerequisite: Complete the preceding layer to unlock this one:
stem.dissection.predict_how_size_depth_c: Predict how size, depth, care, or time pressure will change the modeled outcome...
stem.dissection.explain_how_the_four_inp: Explain how the four inputs affect the model, then name one limitation...
